title: Stage 0: encoder data curve on diverse teacher corpus

notes:
Corpus expanded to five visual domains for style robustness (Max): 96-clip photoreal (jewels_diverse_v1, seeds 50000+) plus four 36-clip style passes over the same prompt subset — anime 60000, 2D cartoon 61000, 3D render 62000, claymation 63000 — chained to run automatically after the photoreal harvest (run_style_passes.sh). 240 clips total. Rationale: the cel gate proved fitted-jewel behavior is domain-dependent (flat-region error -35.7%, contour +62.3%), so a photoreal-only encoder would bake an unmeasured domain prior into every later stage; stylized content is also where licensed-character work would live. G1 to be reported per style, not just macro.
PROTOCOL NOTE (2026-08-18): the data curve must hold the validation set FIXED across every curve point, varying only training corpus size. A pipelined partial-corpus run (46 train / 6 held-out across 12 diverse classes) reaches 21.71 dB at step 2500 and rising — NOT comparable to the 23.41 dB LTX-domain result, whose validation was 4 clips of the 4 classes it trained on. Curve design: freeze one validation set (one eval clip per class per style, ~17 clips at full corpus), then train points at 12/25/50/100/200 training windows against that same set; report G1 per style. The partial run stands as an early 'encoder handles diverse content' signal, not a curve point.
Curve v1 STOPPED after 2 points — protocol invalid, recorded as a lesson. Fixed 6000-step budget across points made per-window exposure vary 15x (n=12: ~500 passes/window; n=180: ~33), so n=12 overfit (peak 21.857 at step 4000, declining to 21.797) while n=180 rose monotonically and was truncated still-climbing at 22.380. The measured +0.58 dB for 15x data is a lower bound set by the step budget, NOT saturation. Frozen step budgets are correct for model comparisons, wrong for data curves — use matched epochs or train-to-convergence. SURVIVING FINDING: per-style spread at n=180 is 4.8 dB (render3d 24.51, clay 23.67, photoreal 22.32, cartoon 21.71, anime 19.70). Anime lagging independently reproduces the cel gate: flat regions + sharp ink contours are the hard case for Gaussians — an allocation problem (see jewels-v2o), not a data problem. Style diversity in the corpus surfaced this immediately; macro-only reporting would have hidden it. Evidence: sol/results/amortized_encoder_v0/corpus_curve_v1.

title: Path B epic: jewels as descriptions, not samples
description: DECISION (Max, 2026-08-18): pursue jewels that describe content rather than sample video. Evidence forcing this: an ablation showed the amortized encoder's learned features contribute only 0.15 dB at inference (real-seed/mean-cells 14.561 vs both-real 14.709 dB, while real-cells/mean-seed collapses to 12.205, BELOW the both-mean 12.343 control). The encoder's quality comes from its seeded initialization — sample video colors onto a fixed lattice with globally-learned sizes — so its jewel field is a re-encoded video, and cell quantization looked lossless (2048 tokens, -0.05 dB) only because the quantized half carries almost nothing. That format cannot support the LLM-emission vision: tokenizing it reduces to tokenizing a coarse video. The fitter by contrast produces content-adaptive fields (median anisotropy ~3 on real footage, densified on content) which ARE descriptive. Goal: an encoder whose jewels must describe — far fewer jewels (thousands not 73k), no direct color copying, a genuine bottleneck forcing summarization rather than lookup. Success means a few thousand jewels reconstruct a window well, which simultaneously delivers real compression, meaningful tokens, and the order-free emission property (each jewel carries its own u,v,t).
notes: Path B v1 COMPLETE — controlled pair on the same 10,240-jewel structural encoder (quaternion+scale shape, no colour lookup, free positions). RENDER-ONLY: structure degrades monotonically as quality rises (extent IQR 2.10@1k -> 1.31@8k; uniformity 0.9961 -> 0.9994, marginally WORSE than the lattice encoder it replaced; anisotropy ~4.3). Mechanism: L2 rewards adequate coverage everywhere, so clustering starves flat regions — uniform tiling is the optimum and SGD finds it; the fitter escapes only via densify/prune outside the loss. DISTILLED (symmetric Chamfer on positions + scale-invariant anisotropy-spread matching vs fitted fields): quality rises while structure HOLDS or IMPROVES — anisotropy 6.29 (61% of fitter's 10.25, vs 4.28 render-only), extent IQR 1.84 (81% of 2.28), uniformity 0.9909 and falling (first run ever to move toward the fitter's 0.946). CONCLUSION: feed-forward content-adaptive fields are achievable; the obstacle was the OBJECTIVE, not the architecture. Shape adaptation largely solved in one forward pass vs 9000 optimization steps/clip. Placement only partly solved (uniformity 0.9909 vs 0.946) — leading hypothesis is that the 12,000-jewel teacher subsample is ~1:1 with the 10,240 student so coverage is satisfiable without migration; test with a sparser teacher target and/or freer position bounds.
